text: When I was twenty seven, I was a clerk for a mining broker in San Francisco, and I knew everything about the stock market. <break time="0.8s" /> I was alone in the world, and I had nothing to depend on except my wits and my good name. <break time="0.8s" /> One Saturday afternoon I went sailing on the bay, but a strong wind carried my little boat far out to sea. <break time="0.8s" /> Just at nightfall, a small ship bound for London picked me up, and I worked as a common sailor to pay for my passage. <break time="0.8s" /> When I stepped ashore in London, my clothes were ragged, and I had only one dollar in my pocket. <break time="0.8s" /> That dollar fed and sheltered me for twenty four hours, but during the next day I had no food and no place to sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> The next morning, as I dragged myself along Portland Place, a child threw a big, juicy pear with only one bite gone into the gutter. <break time="0.8s" /> I stopped and fixed my hungry eyes on that pear, but every time I moved toward it, someone passing by looked at me. <break time="0.8s" /> I was just desperate enough to grab it when a window behind me opened, and a gentleman called out, Step in here, please. <break time="0.8s" /> If he had not called to me at that very moment, I would have taken the pear in front of everyone.
